instructions: Rub the vinegar over the roast, then rub the salt and pepper over all sides.
Chop the ham, onion, bell pepper, 1 of the carrots, the garlic, the olives, the capers and 1 tbsp parsley. Mix them in a bowl with the oregano.
With a long thin knife, cut six slits evenly around the roast, each going halfway into the meat. Push an equal share of the filling into each slit.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat. Brown the roast for 4 minutes a side, until deep brown all over.
Add the broth and tomato sauce and bring it to a boil. Turn the heat to low, cover and cook for 2 hours, turning the roast once halfway through.
Cut the potatoes and the other 4 carrots into chunks. Add them to the pot, cover and cook for 30 minutes, until the roast is fork-tender and the vegetables are soft.
Transfer the roast to a board and let it rest for 10 minutes. Slice it across the grain, keeping the filling in each slice.
Let any leftovers cool, then keep the meat and vegetables in the cooking liquid in the fridge for 4 days or in the freezer for 3 months. Reheat gently in the liquid.
Serve sliced, with the potatoes, carrots and the cooking liquid spooned over.
method_notes: Hawaiian Electric's Carne Mechada (stuffed meat) leads: a boneless roast with a ham, onion, olive and caper filling pushed into a deep slit, browned, then simmered in tomato sauce for 2 1/2 hours with potatoes and carrots. Margarita's International Recipes agrees on a ham, olive, onion and pepper filling in several cuts and a 2 hour simmer in beef stock. The list promises a braise in wine, but none of the pages used wine, so none is added; the liquid is broth and tomato sauce. The salt pork in the lead is left out and the filling stays ham only. No rating appeared, so this is a fallback.
